item.title: 3rd Chinese Peacekeeping Quick Reaction Force to Abyei passes UN military capability assessment
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
By Zhang Zhikang, Yang Biao, Deng Yifan, Gu Chong, Zhang Xuhao and Tan Chaobo Chinese peacekeepers arrive at the mission site and establish a security perimeter and defensive positions during an emergency response and reinforcement drill. ABYEI, Sept. 29 -- The 3rd Chinese Peacekeeping Quick Reaction Force to the United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA) recently underwent a UNISFA military capability assessment. The UNISFA military capability assessment is primarily aimed at assessing the peacekeeping force's ability to carry out mandated missions and effectively respond to various emergencies. During the assessment, the evaluation team examined and assessed more than 120 items in 11 areas, including combat readiness training, personnel administration, civil-military coordination, and logistics support. The quick reaction force received an excellent rating in all assessment items and successfully passed its first assessment. The UNISFA evaluation team listens to a briefing on the development of the Chinese peacekeeping quick reaction force's military capabilities. UNISFA evaluators review records and materials related to logistics support. UNISFA environmental management personnel conducts an on-site inspection of camp facilities. Chinese peacekeepers rapidly disembark and establish a security perimeter and defensive positions during an emergency response and reinforcement drill. Chinese peacekeepers disembark and take up defensive positions during a riot-control drill.

item.title: China Coast Guard patrols waters east of Taiwan Island
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
BEIJING, Sept. 29 (Xinhua) -- The China Coast Guard (CCG) on Tuesday conducted routine law-enforcement patrols in the waters east of China's Taiwan Island in accordance with the law, a spokesperson said. Jiang Lue, a spokesperson for the CCG, said that a CCG task group led by the ship Zhujiajian has been strengthening control over the relevant waters since September. This is to effectively ensure orderly navigation and activities, and to safeguard the legitimate rights and interests, as well as the lives and property of Chinese people on both sides of the Taiwan Strait. The CCG will continue to strengthen law-enforcement patrols in the waters under China's jurisdiction and resolutely safeguard China's territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests, the spokesperson said. CCG task groups have maintained routine patrols in the relevant waters over recent months. Also on Tuesday, a spokesperson of the CCG Donghai Branch said the coast guard of east China's Fujian Province has conducted routine law-enforcement patrols in accordance with the law in the waters near Kinmen since the beginning of September. Task groups have been dispatched to strengthen control and management over relevant waters, said Zhu Anqing, adding that the move is an effective step to protect the legitimate rights and interests, as well as the lives and property of fishermen on both sides of the Taiwan Strait, and to ensure orderly navigation and activities. Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu are all parts of China. Law enforcement patrols carried out by the mainland coast guard in the relevant waters are reasonable and lawful, and are conducive to maintaining maritime operational order and protecting people from both sides of the Taiwan Strait.

item.title: China's top diplomat urges Japan to correct erroneous words, deeds of its leaders on Taiwan question
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
Wang Yi, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and director of the Office of the Foreign Affairs Commission of the CPC Central Committee, meets with Takeshi Iwaya, president of the Japanese Association for the Promotion of International Trade (JAPIT), in Beijing, capital of China, Sept. 28, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu) BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- China's top diplomat Wang Yi on Monday said that for Japan, the pressing task is to correct the erroneous words and deeds of its leaders on the Taiwan question as soon as possible. Wang, director of the Office of the Foreign Affairs Commission of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks when meeting with Takeshi Iwaya, president of the Japanese Association for the Promotion of International Trade (JAPIT) in Beijing. Wang said that the JAPIT has been committed to the cause of China-Japan friendship since its establishment, especially when China-Japan relations face challenges and damage, it still upholds friendly beliefs towards China and safeguard the political foundation of bilateral ties. Noting that this year marks the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trials, Wang said that Japan is once again facing the test of history. If Japan refuses to learn from historical lessons, challenges the post-war pacifist Constitution, denies its history of aggression or glorifies war criminals, it cannot face the world and there's no building a future to speak of. Next year marks the 55th anniversary of the normalization of diplomatic relations between China and Japan. What matters is to adopt a correct attitude on historical issues. Fundamentally, Japan needs to develop an objective and rational perception of China, he added. It is hoped that the JAPIT and all insightful people will carry forward the tradition of friendship, push Japan to make the right choice and deliver a satisfactory answer, Wang said. Iwaya said that the current state of Japan-China relations is concerning. The JAPIT will carry forward the legacy of its former president Yohei Kono and work to bring bilateral relations back to the original intent and starting point of the four political documents between Japan and China. He said Japan should not forget the lessons of the past, and Japanese politicians must steer the country in the right direction and remain firmly committed to the path of peaceful development.

item.title: China firmly opposes any action of Philippines to harm China's sovereignty, rights: FM spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
BEIJING, Sept. 29 (Xinhua) -- China firmly opposes any action of the Philippines that harms China's sovereignty and rights and interests, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Tuesday. Guo made the remarks at a regular press briefing in response to a query related to a so-called updated "maritime chart" by the Philippine National Maritime Council, which includes islands and reefs in China's Nansha Qundao such as Zhongye Dao and Mahuan Dao. "Zhongye Dao and Mahuan Dao are part of China's Nansha Qundao and Chinese territory. China has indisputable sovereignty over Nansha Qundao and its adjacent waters," Guo said. Noting that the scope of Philippine territory is defined by several international treaties, Guo said that China's Nanhai Zhudao, including Nansha Qundao, lie beyond that scope. The Philippines has illegally occupied several islands and reefs in Nansha Qundao, claimed the so-called "Kalayaan Island Group" beyond its own territory and issued a so-called "maritime chart," which includes relevant islands and reefs of China's Nansha Qundao, Guo said. "Those actions seriously violate China's territorial sovereignty and the UN Charter and relevant international laws, and are illegal, null and void," he said. "China firmly opposes any action of the Philippines that harms China's sovereignty and rights and interests. China will continue taking necessary measures to firmly defend its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests in the South China Sea," the spokesperson said.

item.title: Xi to pay tribute to national heroes on Martyrs' Day
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and other Party and state leaders will present flower baskets to fallen national heroes at Tian'anmen Square in central Beijing on Wednesday morning to mark the country's Martyrs' Day. The leaders will be joined by representatives from all walks of life at the ceremony, which will be broadcast live by the China Media Group. In 2014, China's top legislature adopted the decision to establish Martyrs' Day. Observed on Sept. 30, one day before National Day, the day commemorates those who gave their lives for national independence and prosperity. Since the first Martyrs' Day, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, has maintained the tradition of paying homage to fallen heroes on the day. This year marks the 77th founding anniversary of the People's Republic of China and the 105th founding anniversary of the CPC. It also marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March, which lasted from 1934 to 1936. A themed exhibition is being held at the Military Museum of the Chinese People's Revolution in Beijing to commemorate that epic military trek. During the Long March, the CPC-led Red Army soldiers braved raging rivers, snow-covered mountains and treacherous grasslands, with some marching as far as 12,500 kilometers. The arduous journey helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution.
